actor_id.description: ActorID is null for entries the server wrote itself.

details.description:
Details holds the sanitized request, a before snapshot and the changed
fields; its shape depends on the action.

next_before.description:
NextBefore is the value of the before parameter that fetches the next
page; null on the last page.

email.description:
Email is the caller's own address; omitted when none is set. It is never
shown to other members or administrators.

email_verified.description: EmailVerified is true once the address was confirmed by its link.

mail_available.description:
MailAvailable is true when the server can send e-mail (SMTP is
configured): addresses can be confirmed and passwords reset by mail.

recovery_codes_remaining.description:
RecoveryCodesRemaining is how many single-use recovery codes are unused
(0 when two-factor sign-in is off).

two_factor_enabled.description: TwoFactorEnabled is true while sign-in asks for an authenticator code.

avatar_url.description: AvatarURL is the API URL of the avatar (/api/media/{id}); omitted when none.

banned.description: Banned marks a disabled account that was banned (see GET /api/admin/bans).

banner_url.description:
BannerURL is the API URL of the profile banner (/api/media/{id}); omitted
when none and in every payload but the profile endpoints (GET
/api/users/{userID}, GET /api/auth/me and the banner routes).

locale.description: Locale is the chosen UI language ("de", "en"); empty until chosen.

login_locked.description:
LoginLocked is set while wrong passwords lock the account (or a client
address) out in memory. Only the Owner sees it set.

presence.description:
Presence is the chosen presence, only present in responses about the
caller's own account; others see the live one from the hub.

role.description:
Role is "admin" for the Owner (the one account named by ADMIN_USERNAME,
all-powerful and untouchable) and "user" for everybody else; what a user
may do beyond the defaults comes from roles (see GET /api/permissions).

role_ids.description: RoleIDs are the account's custom roles, highest first.

rules_pending.description:
RulesPending is true while the caller has to accept the community rules
(POST /api/onboarding/accept) before posting, reacting, uploading or
joining a Talk. Only set in responses about the caller's own account.

status_text.description: StatusText is a free-text status line; empty when unset.

timeout_until.description: TimeoutUntil is set while the account is timed out.

voice_seconds.description:
Activity totals, filled where they are shown (members, profiles):
time spent in voice rooms (finished stays) and messages sent.

password_reset.description:
PasswordReset is true when members can reset a forgotten password by
e-mail (the server can send mail). It does not say who has an address.

banned_by.description: BannedBy names the moderator; empty when that account is gone.

banned_until.description: BannedUntil is null for a ban without an end.

duration_seconds.description:
DurationSeconds ends the ban by itself after that long (60 seconds to
ten years); null or missing bans for good.

reason.description:
Reason is shown to the member when they try to sign in; send an empty
string for none.

revoke_invite.description:
RevokeInvite also revokes the invite the account registered with, so
that code cannot create the account anew (default true).

code.description: Code is generated (12 characters) when omitted or empty.

expires_in_hours.description: ExpiresInHours never expires when null or omitted.

max_uses.description: MaxUses is unlimited when null or omitted.

code.description:
Code is a current authenticator code or an unused recovery code; needed
only while two-factor sign-in is on.

Code is a current authenticator or recovery code; needed only while
two-factor sign-in is on.

expires_at.description: ExpiresAt is when a ready export stops being downloadable.

next_request_at.description: NextRequestAt is when a new export may be requested; omitted if now.

state.description: State is none, pending, ready, failed, downloaded or expired.

weak.description:
Weak is true for a custom code that is easy to guess (too short, a common
word). New codes like that are refused and old ones no longer work for
sign-up; regenerate them.

token.description: Token is the one from the link in the reset mail.

password.description: Password needs 10 characters at least and 72 bytes at most.

username.description: Username must be unique; "all" and "here" are reserved.

presence.description:
Presence is the chosen presence; "offline" is never chosen, it follows
from having no open WebSocket.

password.description: Password is shown once; it is never stored in plain text.

duration_seconds.description: DurationSeconds is how long the member is silenced, from now.

reason.description: Reason is shown to the member. Optional.

challenge.description:
Challenge is a single-use token bound to the account and to this
sign-in; it is worth nothing without a valid code.

expires_in.description: ExpiresIn is the number of seconds the challenge stays open.

code.description: Code is the six digits the app shows for the new secret.

Code is the six digits of the authenticator app, or an unused recovery
code (spaces and dashes are ignored).

security_notice.description:
SecurityNotice is set once when at least five wrong codes were entered
since the last sign-in.

otpauth_uri.description: OtpauthURI is the same secret as an otpauth:// URI, for the QR code.

secret.description: Secret is the shared secret in base32, for typing into an app by hand.

display_name.description: DisplayName: empty resets it to the username.

avatar_url.description: AvatarURL is the API URL of the avatar (/api/media/{id}); omitted when none.

banner_url.description:
BannerURL is the API URL of the profile banner (/api/media/{id}); omitted
when none and in every payload but the profile endpoints (GET
/api/users/{userID}, GET /api/auth/me and the banner routes).

locale.description: Locale is the chosen UI language ("de", "en"); empty until chosen.

presence.description:
Presence is the chosen presence, only present in responses about the
caller's own account; others see the live one from the hub.

role.description:
Role is "admin" for the Owner (the one account named by ADMIN_USERNAME,
all-powerful and untouchable) and "user" for everybody else; what a user
may do beyond the defaults comes from roles (see GET /api/permissions).

rules_pending.description:
RulesPending is true while the caller has to accept the community rules
(POST /api/onboarding/accept) before posting, reacting, uploading or
joining a Talk. Only set in responses about the caller's own account.

status_text.description: StatusText is a free-text status line; empty when unset.

voice_seconds.description:
Activity totals, filled where they are shown (members, profiles):
time spent in voice rooms (finished stays) and messages sent.

token.description: Token is the one from the link in the confirmation mail.

elevated.description:
Elevated is true when the bot holds Administrator or opens any part of
the admin area: the interface warns about it.

permissions.description: Permissions are the server-wide permissions (a bit set).

allowed_intents.description: AllowedIntents are the gateway intents the bot may ask for.

avatar_url.description: AvatarURL is the API URL of the avatar; omitted when none.

disabled.description: Disabled bots cannot use any token or gateway connection.

role_ids.description:
RoleIDs are the bot's roles, highest first; its permissions come from
them and from channel overwrites, never from @everyone.

type.description:
Type is 4 (reply with a message) or 5 (acknowledge now, answer later
with follow-ups).

builtin.description:
Builtin marks a command the server runs itself (no bot): bot_name is
empty, and running it answers 200 with the result instead of 202.

disabled.description:
Disabled commands are hidden from members and refuse invocations; only
an admin can set it, a bot registering the command again keeps it.

Disabled commands are hidden from members and refuse invocations; only
an admin can set it, a bot registering the command again keeps it.

name.description: Name is lowercase letters, digits, '-' and '_' (1 to 32).

options.description:
Options maps option names to values: a string, a whole number, a
boolean, or the ID of a member or channel.

interaction_id.description: InteractionID identifies the run; the bot answers it.

expires_at.description: ExpiresAt is empty for a token that never expires.

issuer_binding.description:
IssuerBinding is only set for a token issued before 1.0, which has no
recorded issuer: "unbound" until it is first used after the upgrade,
then "inferred" (bound to the bot's creator or the Owner, whoever
qualified; regenerate it to bind it to its real issuer). Absent for a
token whose issuer was recorded when it was issued.

secret.description: Secret is the API token. It is shown only now; only its hash is kept.

choices.description:
Choices limit a string option to these values (the composer shows them
as a list). At most 25, each 1 to 100 characters.

type.description:
Type is Discord's option type: 3 string, 4 integer, 5 boolean, 6 user
(a member's ID), 7 channel (a channel ID).

flags.description:
Flags: 64 makes the response ephemeral, visible only to the member who ran
the command (never stored).

allowed_intents.description: AllowedIntents are the gateway intents the admin allowed.

id.description: ID is the bot's user ID: the author of its messages (user_id).

expires_at.description: ExpiresAt is empty for a token that never expires.

issuer_binding.description:
IssuerBinding is only set for a token issued before 1.0, which has no
recorded issuer: "unbound" until it is first used after the upgrade,
then "inferred" (bound to the bot's creator or the Owner, whoever
qualified; regenerate it to bind it to its real issuer). Absent for a
token whose issuer was recorded when it was issued.

expires_at.description: ExpiresAt is optional; without it the token never expires.

parse.description:
Parse lists the kinds of mentions that notify: "users" and "everyone"
(@all and @here, which also need the Mention everyone permission).
"roles" lets @Role notify the role's members (the role must be
mentionable, or the bot must hold Mention everyone).

roles.description: Roles are role IDs (UUIDs) notified although "roles" is not in Parse.

users.description: Users are user IDs (UUIDs) notified although "users" is not in Parse.

allowed_mentions.description:
AllowedMentions limits who is notified. Default: members mentioned by
@username are, @all and @here are not.

content.description: Content is the message text (Markdown), at most 4000 characters.

message_reference.description: MessageReference quotes a message of the same channel.

parent_id.description: ParentID posts into the thread of a root message of the channel.

bot.description:
Bot is true for bot accounts, which are members too. Mention one by its
username like any member; message.mentions then lists its id.

message_id.description: MessageID is the message to quote; it must be in the same channel.

count.description: Count is how many of their latest messages (replies included), 1 to 100.

reason.description: Reason is kept in the audit log. Optional.

user_id.description: UserID is the member whose latest messages in the channel go.

number.description: Number is the channel's short, stable link number (/c/12-general).

slow_mode_seconds.description:
SlowModeSeconds is the least time between two messages of one member
in this channel; 0 = off. Members who may manage messages here are
exempt.

user_limit.description:
UserLimit is the most members a voice channel admits at once; 0 = no
limit.

user_ids.description:
UserIDs are the other members: one for a conversation with one person,
two to nine for a group.

parent_id.description: ParentID must be a root message of the same channel (thread reply).

reply_to_id.description: ReplyToID must be a message of the same conversation (quoted reply).

category.description: Category is why the message is reported.

note.description: Note is an optional explanation for the moderators, up to 500 characters.

reason.description:
Reason is shown to the author when a moderator deletes their message,
and kept in the audit log. Up to 200 characters.

can_send.description:
CanSend says whether the caller may write in it now: they hold Send
direct messages, the community has direct messages on, and no timeout
or pending rules apply. It says nothing about the other members; a
message that cannot be sent to them is refused when sent.

group.description:
Group is true for a conversation that can take more members; a
conversation with one other person is not.

id.description:
ID is the id messages are read and written under, in the message
routes (/api/channels/{id}/messages), which accept it for members only.

last_message_at.description: LastMessageAt is when the latest message was written (null: none yet).

members.description: Members are everybody in it, the caller included.

unread_count.description:
UnreadCount counts top-level messages of others since the caller last
read it; MentionCount those of them that mention the caller by name or
reply to them.

message_id.description: MessageID is the oldest top-level message by someone else after `since`; null when there is none.
The rest is set only when Available.

channel_id.description: ChannelID is the channel or direct message conversation to forward to.

comment.description: Comment is the forwarder's own text, optional.

category_id.description: CategoryID limits the call to one category's channels; omitted or null means every channel the caller may view.

message_id.description: MessageID is the message to mark read up to; null or omitted means now.

added_by.description: AddedBy is the member who created the bot, when known.

avatar_url.description: AvatarURL is the API URL of the avatar (/api/media/{id}); omitted when none.

banner_url.description:
BannerURL is the API URL of the profile banner (/api/media/{id}); omitted
when none and in every payload but the profile endpoints (GET
/api/users/{userID}, GET /api/auth/me and the banner routes).

is_bot.description:
IsBot is true for a bot account (see doc/bots.md). Bots hold the
built-in Bot role; webhook authors are never listed.

locale.description: Locale is the chosen UI language ("de", "en"); empty until chosen.

presence.description:
Presence is the chosen presence, only present in responses about the
caller's own account; others see the live one from the hub.

role.description:
Role is "admin" for the Owner (the one account named by ADMIN_USERNAME,
all-powerful and untouchable) and "user" for everybody else; what a user
may do beyond the defaults comes from roles (see GET /api/permissions).

role_ids.description: RoleIDs are the member's custom roles, highest first.

rules_pending.description:
RulesPending is true while the caller has to accept the community rules
(POST /api/onboarding/accept) before posting, reacting, uploading or
joining a Talk. Only set in responses about the caller's own account.

status_text.description: StatusText is a free-text status line; empty when unset.

timeout_until.description:
TimeoutUntil is set while the member is timed out: they can read but
not post, react, speak or join Talks.

voice_seconds.description:
Activity totals, filled where they are shown (members, profiles):
time spent in voice rooms (finished stays) and messages sent.

embeds.description: Embeds are the rich cards of a webhook message (Discord-style subset).

forward.description:
Forward is set when the message forwards another one. It says so and
nothing more: no id and no text of the original travels with the
message, because readers differ in what they may see. Each reader gets
the original (with its ids) from GET /api/messages/{id}/forward.

is_bot.description:
IsBot is true for messages posted by a webhook. Their author is a
hidden bot account; DisplayName is the webhook's name or the username
the sender gave for this message.

is_webhook.description:
IsWebhook narrows IsBot: the author is an incoming webhook (shown with
a Webhook label), not a bot account (shown with a BOT label).

mention_roles.description:
MentionRoles are the roles this message mentions (@Role); the client
draws them as role pills. A role that was deleted since drops out. The
server always sends it; it is optional for clients that build messages
themselves (the desktop app's native chat path).

mentions.description: Mentions are the users this message mentions (@username, @all, @here).

number.description: Number is the message's short, stable link number (/m/4821).

poll.description: Poll is set when the message is a poll; its content is the question.

content.description: Content is the text of this earlier version.

edited_at.description:
EditedAt is when this version was written (the message's creation time
for the original).

replaced_at.description: ReplacedAt is when an edit replaced it.

anonymous.description: Anonymous polls never name voters: options carry counts only.

closed.description: Closed is true once ClosesAt has passed, as the server saw it.

closes_at.description: ClosesAt is when voting ends; ending the poll early moves it to that moment.

multiple.description: Multiple lets a member vote for several options.

total_voters.description: TotalVoters counts members who voted for at least one option.

voters.description: Voters is only present when the poll is not anonymous.

dm_policy.description:
DMPolicy is everyone (the default) or nobody. It only decides who can
start a conversation with the caller or add them to a group; existing
conversations go on.

emoji.description: Emoji has no whitespace, control characters, '<' or '>'.

channel_id.description: ChannelID is the channel of the message.

is_bot.description: IsBot and IsWebhook describe the quoted author like Message does.

channel_id.description: ChannelID and ChannelName are left out for a direct message.

note.description: Note is what the reporter wrote.

resolution_note.description: ResolutionNote is the moderator's note on closing the report.

channel_id.description: ChannelID and ChannelName are left out for a direct message.

note.description: Note is what the reporter wrote.

resolution_note.description: ResolutionNote is the moderator's note on closing the report.

context.description:
Context are up to 20 messages of the same channel or conversation
around the reported one, oldest first.

note.description: Note is kept with the report, up to 500 characters.

status.description: Status closes the report: resolved (acted on) or dismissed (no action).

note.description:
Note replaces the note; left out (or null), a saved message keeps its
note and a new one starts without.

available.description:
Available is false when the caller may no longer see the message; then
Message is absent and nothing but the id and the note is sent.

note.description: Note is the caller's own note (up to 200 characters), possibly empty.

roots.description: Roots maps a reply hit's parent_id to its thread root.

snippet.description: Snippet is the start of the root message (at most 200 characters).

muted_until.description: MutedUntil ends a mute (level mute only): in the future, at most a year ahead. Null or omitted mutes until unmuted.

following.description: Following: replies of this thread notify the caller. Servers before 1.1 do not send it.
Following: replies of the thread notify the caller.

thread_id.description: ThreadID is the root message of the thread.

slow_mode_seconds.description:
SlowModeSeconds sets the least time between two messages of one member
in the channel (0 turns slow mode off). Members who may manage messages
in the channel are exempt.

user_limit.description: UserLimit caps a voice channel's members at once; 0 removes the limit.

animated.description: Animated emoji are GIFs and have a still frame for reduced motion.

still_url.description: StillURL is the first frame (animated emoji only).

url.description:
URL serves the image; it changes with the content (the v parameter), so
it may be cached for good.

limit.description: Limit is how many custom emoji the instance allows (EMOJI_MAX).

heartbeat_interval.description:
HeartbeatInterval is the interval the gateway will ask for, in
milliseconds (also in HELLO).

max_connections.description: MaxConnections is how many gateway connections one bot may hold.

url.description: URL is the WebSocket address of the gateway.

code.description: Code is one of the stable Code* constants; clients branch on it.

message.description: Message is a human-readable English message.

code.description:
Code is Discord's JSON error code: 0 for plain HTTP errors, 10003
unknown channel, 10008 unknown message, 50001 missing access, 50006
empty message, 50013 missing permissions, 50035 invalid form body,
40005 request entity too large.

global.description:
Global is true when the bot's overall limit was hit, false for the
limit of one route.

retry_after.description: RetryAfter is the number of seconds to wait.

image.description:
Image is the original absolute image URL; clients load it through the
image proxy because the CSP only allows same-origin images.

deleted.description: Deleted is how many were removed (cleanup only).

version.description: Version is the rules version the member saw (State.RulesVersion).

direct_messages_enabled.description:
DirectMessagesEnabled is the community's switch for direct messages
(default on). Off: existing conversations stay readable and members
can neither start new ones nor write in them.

rules_text.description: RulesText is Markdown. Empty means no rules: nothing is enforced.

rules_version.description:
RulesVersion counts the published versions of the rules (0: never set).
Members must have accepted it before they may post, react, upload or
join a Talk (only while RulesText is not empty).

start_channel_id.description:
StartChannelID is the text channel new members land in; null for the
first channel they can see.

welcome_text.description: WelcomeText is Markdown, shown to new members first.

direct_messages_enabled.description:
DirectMessagesEnabled switches direct messages on or off for the
community; left out, it stays as it is.

require_reacceptance.description:
RequireReacceptance raises the rules version, so every member (the Owner
excepted) has to accept the rules again. The first time rules are
written the version is raised on its own. Ignored while the rules are
empty.

dismissed_tips.description: DismissedTips are the tips the member closed.

rules_accepted_version.description: RulesAcceptedVersion is the version the member accepted last.

rules_pending.description:
RulesPending is true while the member has to accept the rules; until
then posting, reacting, uploading and joining a Talk answer
RULES_NOT_ACCEPTED. Never true for the Owner.

rules_version.description: RulesVersion is the version in force; 0 while there are no rules.

start_channel_id.description:
StartChannelID is the channel to open after the welcome flow; null when
none is set or the member cannot view it.

welcome_done.description: WelcomeDone is true once the member finished the welcome flow.

dismissed_tips.description: DismissedTips are tip ids to add (at most 32 per call, 64 stored).

welcome_done.description: WelcomeDone marks the welcome flow finished.

count.description: Count is how often it was raised since then (for runtime warnings).

since.description: Since is when the warning was first raised in this process.

value.description: Value is an optional non-sensitive number (e.g. the UDP port count).

channel.description:
Channel permissions can be overwritten per category and channel; the
rest only apply server-wide.

id.description: ID is the role's or the member's ID; the @everyone role is a role.

type.description: Type is what ID refers to.

bot_user_id.description:
BotUserID is set on a bot's own managed role: the account of the one bot
that holds it. The role is named after the bot and goes with it.

max_upload_mb.description:
MaxUploadMB overrides the upload limit of this role's members; null
inherits the global limit. A member gets the highest override of their
roles (@everyone included), never above the server's ceiling.

MaxUploadMB: absent leaves it alone, null inherits the global limit, a
number sets the role's limit. Only the Owner may send it.

ceiling_mb.description: CeilingMB is the operator's hard ceiling (MAX_UPLOAD_SIZE_MB).

max_upload_mb.description: MaxUploadMB is the effective global limit.

anonymous.description: Anonymous hides who voted for what, from everyone.

duration.description: Duration is how long voting stays open; 24h when omitted.

multiple.description: Multiple lets members vote for several options.

anonymous.description: Anonymous polls never name voters: options carry counts only.

closed.description: Closed is true once ClosesAt has passed, as the server saw it.

closes_at.description: ClosesAt is when voting ends; ending the poll early moves it to that moment.

multiple.description: Multiple lets a member vote for several options.

my_votes.description: MyVotes are the options the caller voted for (also in an anonymous poll).

total_voters.description: TotalVoters counts members who voted for at least one option.

option_ids.description: OptionIDs replace the caller's votes; an empty list withdraws them.

enabled.description: Enabled is false when the operator turned push off (PUSH_ENABLED=false).

max_devices.description: MaxDevices is how many devices one account may enable push on.

preview.description: Preview is the member's choice: include the message text in pushes. Only takes effect while PreviewAllowed.

preview_allowed.description: PreviewAllowed is false when the operator forces pushes without message text.

public_key.description: PublicKey is the VAPID public key (base64url) to subscribe with; empty while push is off.

preview.description: Preview includes the message text in pushes (default true).

auth.description: Auth is the browser's 16 byte authentication secret, base64url.

endpoint.description: Endpoint is the push service address the browser got. https only, a public host, port 443.

label.description: Label names the device in the list ("Firefox on Windows"); at most 64 characters.

p256dh.description: P256dh is the browser's P-256 public key, base64url.

role_ids.description: RoleIDs are all custom roles the member should have.

channels.description:
Channels lists every channel the caller may view with what they may do
there (bits).

direct_messages_enabled.description:
DirectMessagesEnabled is the community's switch for direct messages;
CanStartDirectMessages says whether the caller may start them and write
in them now (the switch is on, they hold Send direct messages, and no
timeout or pending rules apply).

max_upload_mb.description:
MaxUploadMB is the largest file the caller may upload, in MB: their
roles' override or the global limit, never above the server's ceiling.
It changes with permissions_changed.

owner.description:
Owner is true for the Owner, who may do everything and cannot be
restricted.

permissions.description: Permissions are the server-wide permissions (bits, see catalog).

role_ids.description: RoleIDs are the caller's custom roles, highest first.

rules_pending.description:
RulesPending is set while the caller has to accept the community rules
(POST /api/onboarding/accept); posting, reacting, uploading and joining
a Talk answer RULES_NOT_ACCEPTED until then.

timeout_until.description:
TimeoutUntil and TimeoutReason are set while the caller is timed out:
they can read but not post, react, speak or join Talks. The reason is
the moderator's, and the caller's own to see.

top_position.description:
TopPosition is the position of the caller's highest role (0 without
one); the Owner is above every position. A member can only manage roles
and members below it.

role_ids.description:
RoleIDs lists every custom role (not @everyone) exactly once, highest
first.

max_upload_mb.description: MaxUploadMB is the new global limit; null returns to the server's ceiling.

latest_migration.description: LatestMigration is the newest applied migration file, e.g. "0012_message_count.sql".

pending_migrations.description:
PendingMigrations counts embedded migrations not applied yet (0 when
the server started normally: it migrates before serving).

features.description:
Features lists the optional features this server has, so a web app of a
newer release can hide what an older server lacks (for example "blocks").
A server of 1.0.x sends no list. See doc/api-stability.md.

web_client_api.description: WebClientAPI identifies the HTTPS web-client desktop integration contract.

credential.description: Credential is set for TURN only and valid for 12 hours.

username.description: Username is set for TURN only.

media_retention_days.description: MediaRetentionDays is 0 when media is kept until deleted manually.

update_check.description:
UpdateCheck is true when the server asks GitHub for new releases
(UPDATE_CHECK_ENABLED); the privacy policy then names the connection.

configured.description: Configured is true when SMTP_HOST is set.

from.description: From is the sender address of outgoing mail; empty when not configured.

tls.description: TLS is the transport security in use (starttls, tls or none); empty when not configured.

waited.description: Waited counts acquisitions that had to wait for a free connection.

cpu_millicores.description: CPUMillicores is process CPU use over the interval, 1000 = one core.

t.description: T is the unix time in seconds.

history.description: History holds up to the last hour of samples, oldest first.

interval_seconds.description: IntervalSeconds is the spacing of History.

mem_alloc_bytes.description:
MemAllocBytes is live heap memory; MemSysBytes what the Go runtime
obtained from the OS.

password.description: Password is the admin's current password (re-authentication).

target_version.description:
TargetVersion must equal the latest release the server knows, so a
dialog opened before a newer release can't start the wrong update.

available.description:
Available: configured, an update exists, the image can reach it and no
update ran in the last five minutes.

configured.description: Configured is true when UPDATER_TOKEN is set (sidecar opted in).

image.description: Image is MNEMA_IMAGE, the image reference the app container runs.

next_allowed_at.description: NextAllowedAt is set during the cooldown after an update request.

reach.description: Reach says whether re-pulling Image can reach the latest release.

mail.description: Mail is the outgoing mail setup (account e-mails need it).

warnings.description:
Warnings are configuration or deployment problems the server noticed

info.description:
REST API of Mnema Talk, a self-hosted, invite-only chat and voice app for a single community.
Authentication is an HttpOnly session cookie set by login/register. State-changing requests (anything but GET/HEAD/OPTIONS) must carry a same-origin Origin header, otherwise 403.
JSON bodies are decoded strictly: unknown fields are rejected with 400 and bodies are limited to 1 MiB. Errors share the ErrorResponse shape.
Everything except the SPA assets lives under /api.
Conventions. Creating returns 201 with the new object; a delete or a change without a result returns 204 with no body, while a few operations return 200 with the changed object (for example timing out a member or unpinning a message), as their descriptions say.
Every 429 carries a Retry-After header (seconds). Lists that page do so with `limit` and, depending on the list, `before` / `after` (an id) or a cursor; each operation names its parameters and maximum.
Uploads are the one exception to the 1 MiB body limit; their size limits are on the operations.
A 403 names its cause in the message: a missing permission (named on the operation), a role that is not below yours, or a cross-origin request refused by the Origin / Sec-Fetch-Site check.
A 403 with the code RULES_NOT_ACCEPTED means the member has not accepted the community rules yet. It is returned by every operation that posts, reacts, uploads or joins a Talk (sending messages and polls, voting, reactions, uploads, slash commands); accept the rules with POST /api/onboarding/accept first.

get.description:
Upgrades to a WebSocket (requires a same-origin Origin header; a foreign origin is refused with 403 by the upgrade handler). OpenAPI cannot model WebSocket frames, so the protocol is described here.

Every frame in both directions is a JSON text message `{"type": string, "payload": any}`. At most a few events per second per connection (and per account across its connections) are processed; excess client events, and events whose payload is over the cap for their type (1 KiB, more only for an SDP answer, ICE candidate, diagnostic and media handshake), are dropped.

Server to client, on connect (to this connection only):
- `presence_snapshot`: map of user id to live status for every online user.
- `voice_snapshot`: map of voice channel id to a map of user id to User plus `joined_at`.
- `voice_rooms`: `{started: {channelId: time}, now}`; the server clock lets clients count up.

Server to client, broadcast to all connections:
Channel events (`message_*`, `typing`, `voice_state_update`, `webrtc_media_state`) only reach connections whose user may view that channel; the connect snapshots list only the Talks the user may view.
- `message_create`, `message_update`: Message.
- `message_delete`: `{id, channel_id, parent_id}`.
- `message_reaction`: `{message_id, channel_id, reactions}`.
- `channels_changed`: no payload; refetch GET /api/channels (sent after any category/channel/layout admin change).
- `permissions_changed`: no payload; refetch GET /api/permissions and GET /api/channels. Sent to the users whose roles or permissions may have changed (everybody after a channel, category, overwrite or @everyone change).
- `roles_changed`: no payload; refetch GET /api/roles and GET /api/members (a role was created, edited, deleted, reordered or assigned).
- `emoji_changed`: no payload; refetch GET /api/emoji (a custom emoji was added, renamed or deleted).
- `member_joined`: public User of a newly registered member.
- `user_update`: public User after a profile, status or avatar change, or `{id, disabled}` when an admin disables or enables an account.
- `user_stats`: `{user_id, voice_seconds}` after a voice stay ends.
- `presence_update`: `{user_id, status}` where status is online, away, dnd, focus or offline; for a bot that set an activity also `activity: {type, name}` (Discord activity type).
- `voice_state_update`: `{action: "join", channel_id, user, started_at}` or `{action: "leave", channel_id, user_id}`.
- `typing`: `{channel_id, user_id}` (to everyone except the typist).

Server to client, targeted:
- `block_updated`: to the user's own sessions only; `{user_id, blocked}` after they blocked or unblocked a member (refetch GET /api/me/blocks). The blocked member is never told.
- `dm_created`: to every member's sessions; the direct message (`DirectMessage`) a conversation was started with, or the one the receiver was just added to.
- `dm_member_added`: to the other members of a group conversation; `{dm_id, member}`.
- `dm_member_removed`: to the remaining members and the leaver's sessions; `{dm_id, member}`.
- `read_state`: to the user's own sessions only; `{channel_id, last_read_at, unread_count, mention_count}`, `{channel_id, last_read_at, refresh: true}`, or `{refresh: true}` alone after a notification setting changed or everything was marked read (reload read states and notification settings).
- `webrtc_media_state`: `{channel_id, user_id, screen, camera}` to voice-room members.
- `voice_speaking`: `{channel_id, user_id, active}` to voice-room members, only when the state changes.
- `screen_viewers`: `{channel_id, user_id, viewers}` to voice-room members: `viewers` are the distinct users in the room watching `user_id`'s screen share (sorted ids, never the sharer). Sent whenever that set changes (`viewers: []` once when a watched share ends or loses its last viewer), and on `voice_join` one per live share to the joining connection only.
- `webrtc_offer` (SDP offer), `webrtc_candidate` (ICE candidate): SFU signalling.
- `screen_layers`: `{channel_id, user_id, layers}` to voice-room members: the layers of `user_id`'s live screen share, best first, each `{width, height, fps}` as the sharer declared them. Sent when they change, as an empty list once the share ends, and on `voice_join` one per live share to the joining connection only. A share of a client without layers has none.
- `screen_quality`: `{channel_id, user_id, layer, auto}` to the watching connection only: the layer of `user_id`'s screen share it receives now (`-1` before the first picture) and whether the server chooses it (`auto`).
- `screen_layers_wanted`: `{channel_id, layers}` to the sharing connection only: the indexes of its layers some viewer receives or is about to. A sender may stop encoding the others; layer 0 is always listed while nobody watches.
- `media_handshake`: `{channel_id, user_id, wire}` to the other connections in that voice room. `wire` is opaque: the server checks only its framing (an MLS key package, welcome or public message, or a heartbeat or capability message) and never reads or logs the content.
- `voice_kicked`: `{channel_id, reason?}` when a moderator removes the user from voice, `reason: "room_full"` when a voice join is refused because the room is full (the channel's `user_limit`), `reason: "rules_not_accepted"` when the community's rules have not been accepted yet (POST /api/onboarding/accept), or `reason: "missing_permission"` when the user may not (or no longer may) view and connect to that Talk.
- `pong`: `{t}` echoing a `ping`.

Client to server:
- `ping` `{t}`; `presence_idle` `{idle: bool}`.
- `typing` `{channel_id}` (text and voice channels, rate-limited; ignored without View channels and Send messages).
- `voice_join` `{channel_id}` (needs View channels and Connect, otherwise `voice_kicked` with `reason: "missing_permission"`); `voice_leave`; `voice_speaking` `{active}`. The SFU drops audio without Speak and camera/screen without Video.
- `webrtc_answer` (SDP answer), `webrtc_candidate` (ICE candidate), `webrtc_request_keyframe`.
- `media_handshake` `{channel_id, wire}`: opaque handshake bytes for the current voice room.
- `webrtc_subscribe` `{kind: "screen"|"camera", user_id, on}` or `{kind: "camera", all: true, on}`. A screen subscription may carry `quality`: `"auto"` or the index of a layer (0 is the best); it is applied before the first picture and again whenever sent. Without one, or with `"auto"`, the server chooses: it starts on the best layer, moves down one layer at a time when the viewer's receiver reports show lasting loss, a rising round trip time or repeated keyframe requests, and tries one layer up again after a long stretch without trouble (a failed attempt makes the next one wait twice as long).
- `webrtc_layers` `{layers: [{width, height, fps}, ...]}` (1 to 3, best first, strictly shrinking): the layers of the sender's own screen share. They are sent on the SFU's lower video lines.
- `webrtc_screenshare_stop`, `webrtc_camera_stop`.

Unknown event types are ignored. The server closes the connection when the session is revoked (sign-out of that session, sign-out everywhere, password change) or expires, or the account is disabled. A user keeps at most 8 browser connections: a newer one closes the oldest with close code 4001 ("too many connections"), after which that client should not reconnect by itself. Upgrades are rate-limited per address and per user (429), and `voice_join` beyond about one per second (burst 3) is answered with `voice_kicked`.
